extracted.intended_audience: researchers, small businesses, industry applicants, and other organizations seeking DOE wind energy research & development funding
extracted.subtask_description: Page-level guidance and procedural notes about Wind Energy Technologies Office (IESO/WETO) funding opportunities: what the office funds, what it does not fund, where to find official solicitations, deadlines, and pathways to partner with DOE national labs or apply to related programs (e.g., SBIR/STTR).

rubrics_metrics.name: IESO program focus and funding mechanism
rubrics_metrics.description: The Integrated Energy Systems Office (IESO) focuses on technological development to improve the reliability and affordability of wind energy and addressing barriers to wind energy deployment. IESO funds research and development activities through competitive solicitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects and proposals should align with technological development priorities (reliability, affordability, deployment barriers) and be prepared for competitive solicitation processes rather than guaranteed awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: IESO does not fund purchase or installation of wind energy systems
rubrics_metrics.description: IESO does not fund the purchase or installation of wind energy systems by individuals or companies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants seeking funding for purchase or installation should consult other federal grants and tax incentives; see the Related Opportunities page for those programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: EERE Exchange is the official source for solicitation details
rubrics_metrics.description: Although IESO attempts to maintain current information on these solicitations, the official source for funding information is EERE Exchange.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must consult EERE Exchange for authoritative solicitation documents, requirements, and updates rather than relying solely on this summary page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicitation open and close dates / application windows
rubrics_metrics.description: Each solicitation lists an Open Date and Close Date (e.g., i2x Interconnection Cost Reduction Solutions for Transmission (iCRS-T) — May 5, 2026 to June 18, 2026).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals must be submitted within the posted open/close windows. For historical solicitations, view the Past Opportunities page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pathway to partner with DOE national labs
rubrics_metrics.description: For more opportunities, read about how to partner with the Department of Energy's national labs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants seeking lab collaboration or lab-embedded resources should follow DOE guidance on partnering with national labs (link provided) to structure proposals and engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subscribe for updates
rubrics_metrics.description: Subscribe to the Integrated Energy Insider to receive the latest news, updates, and opportunities from the Integrated Energy Systems Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staying subscribed ensures timely awareness of new solicitations, notices of funding opportunities, and program announcements relevant to proposal development.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBIR/STTR program purpose and eligibility hint
rubrics_metrics.description: The Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR) and Small Business Technology Transfer (STTR) programs offer competitively awarded grants to small businesses to support scientific excellence and technological innovation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small businesses should consult the specific Notice of Funding Opportunity (e.g., FY2025 Phase 1, Release 2) for eligibility, award phases, and application instructions; these are competitive grants targeting small business innovation.
